x: Animated SVG and Lottie from Adobe Animate Flash2SVG is a panel for Adobe Animate. It turns your timelines into animated SVG files that play in every browser — also as a plain img — and into Lottie files for apps. Tweens keep Animate's exact easing; symbols, shape tweens, masks, filters, buttons and sounds come along. # What it does Every way to animate SVG SMIL for anywhere (even img and e-mail clients that show SVG), CSS for pages you style, a 15 KB JS player with Flash's own behaviour, still frames, GIF and WebP fallbacks. Lottie and dotLottie The same timeline for lottie-web, the dotLottie players, Skottie and the iOS, Android, Flutter and React Native players. Exactly like Animate Every tween is checked against Animate's own frames. Classic and custom eases, motion tweens and guides, shape tweens as real morphs. Interactive Buttons, frame scripts ( stop() , gotoAndPlay() ), the Code Snippets panel's mouse handlers, start on click, hover, scroll or when visible. Small files One drawing per symbol, curves instead of frames, images in WebP or AVIF and scaled to what is shown, sounds as MP3 or Opus — and a size overview after every export. Your FLA stays untouched The export works on a temporary copy. HTML5 Canvas documents work as well as ActionScript 3. # Start here Install the panel in Animate 2022 or later. Export your first animation — it takes a minute. Choose a format for where the animation will play. Already exporting? Look up a setting in the settings reference , see what is exported , or put the result on a web page . Note Every animation in this guide was made in Animate and exported with Flash2SVG: what you see is what the panel writes. Each demo has tabs for the formats and a download button for the file. # A few numbers Shape tweens as morphs the morph test document: 105 KB as SMIL instead of 339 KB frame by frame The JS player s runtime 15.2 KB (with sounds 18.7 KB), only in files that need it A 12-megapixel photo shown at 20 % 1042 KB → 100 KB as JPEG, 13 KB as AVIF 150 tweened symbols about 110 frames a second in the JS player Export of a typical scene well under a second after Animate hands over the drawing Flash2SVG is open source (MIT). Version 4 is a ground-up rewrite of Tom Byrne s Flash2Svg for current Animate versions.

Installation Flash2SVG is a panel (a CEP extension) for Adobe Animate 2022 or later on Windows and macOS. It is tested with Animate 2024 (24.0.x) on Windows. Animate 2024 is the current version: Adobe keeps it in maintenance, with security and bug fixes. Download the latest release from the releases page . It has three files: File What it is Flash2SVG- version .zxp The panel, signed. Install it with an extension manager (below). Flash2SVG- version .zip The same panel unpacked, for a manual install. flash2svg-cli.zip The command line compiler , for re-exporting without Animate. # Install the signed ZXP Pick one of these tools: Anastasiy s Extension Manager ( install.anastasiy.com ), free for Windows and macOS: open it, choose Animate , click Install and pick the .zxp . Adobe s own installer (Unified Plugin Installer Agent), which comes with the Creative Cloud app. On Windows, in a terminal: "C:\Program Files\Common Files\Adobe\Adobe Desktop Common\RemoteComponents\UPI\UnifiedPluginInstallerAgent\UnifiedPluginInstallerAgent.exe" / install " $HOME \Downloads\Flash2SVG-4.3.0.zxp" On macOS: "/Library/Application Support/Adobe/Adobe Desktop Common/RemoteComponents/UPI/UnifiedPluginInstallerAgent/UnifiedPluginInstallerAgent.app/Contents/MacOS/UnifiedPluginInstallerAgent" --install ~/Downloads/Flash2SVG-4.3.0.zxp ZXPInstaller , an open-source alternative. Then restart Animate and open the panel: Window › Extensions › Flash2SVG (SVG Animation) . It opens as a floating window; drag its tab into any dock, and Animate remembers the place. Animate 2024 with the hero demo, the document most screenshots in this guide come from. # Install the zip by hand Unzip the archive into Adobe s extension folder, as a folder called org.flash2svg : System Folder Windows %APPDATA%\Adobe\CEP\extensions\org.flash2svg macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Adobe/CEP/extensions/org.flash2svg A panel installed this way is not signed, so Animate loads it only when CEP s debug mode is on — once per machine: reg add HKCU\Software\Adobe\CSXS. 12 / v PlayerDebugMode / t REG_SZ / d 1 / f On macOS: defaults write com.adobe.CSXS.12 PlayerDebugMode 1 . Animate 2022 and 2023 use CSXS.11 instead of CSXS.12 . Tip Prefer the signed ZXP: debug mode lets Animate load any unsigned extension, not only this one. # Update Install the new ZXP over the old one (the extension manager replaces it) and restart Animate. Your settings stay: they are kept per user, and optionally inside each FLA ( Remember settings in the FLA ). # Remove it safely Close the Flash2SVG panel and quit Animate before you remove the extension. Careful Animate 2024 remembers which panels were open in its workspace. If the extension of a remembered panel is gone, Animate quits as soon as a document window opens. If that happened to you: install the extension again, start Animate, close the panel, quit Animate, and only then remove it. # The command line compiler The panel s compiler also runs in Node.js (version 24 or later) on any system: it re-exports a scene the panel extracted, with other settings, without Animate. Unpack flash2svg-cli.zip anywhere and run node flash2svg.js --help . See Command line .

h: 1. Open the panel and your document
x: Your first export This takes about a minute. You need Animate with the panel installed and any FLA with an animation — ActionScript 3 or HTML5 Canvas. # 1. Open the panel and your document Open the FLA, then Window › Extensions › Flash2SVG (SVG Animation) . The panel shows the document s name at the top and its settings below, in sections you can fold. The panel with its default settings. Go to the timeline you want to export — the main timeline of a scene, or a symbol you are editing. Source: Current timeline exports exactly what you see there. # 2. Pick a format In Output , choose how the SVG should animate. If you are unsure, take SMIL : it plays everywhere, even as a plain img . The formats page compares them all. If the animation… choose just plays (a hero, an icon, a logo) SMIL — or Automatic to let Flash2SVG pick has buttons, sounds or code snippets JS player goes into an app (iOS, Android, Flutter) Lottie or .lottie goes into an e-mail GIF or WebP Leave the file name empty to save next to the FLA ( hero.fla → hero.svg ), or type a path. # 3. Export Press Export . The panel copies your document (your FLA is never changed), reads the timeline, and writes the file. A bar shows the progress; Cancel stops it. When it is done, the Result section shows a preview you can play and scrub, the file size, and what the size is made of: The Result section after an export. Open in browser shows the file in your default browser. Show file opens its folder. The coloured bar splits the size into Drawing , Animation , Images , Sounds , Fonts , the Player script and Linked files (written next to the SVG); hover a part for its exact size. Biggest drawings names the symbols worth simplifying first — see Performance . Warnings list what could not be reproduced exactly, and why. Each is worth a look. # 4. Put it on a page An SMIL or CSS file works like any image: < img src = "hero.svg" alt = "Our product in motion" width = "640" height = "360" > The JS player needs a document of its own, so use object (or paste the SVG into the page): < object data = "hero.svg" type = "image/svg+xml" width = "640" height = "360" >Our product in motion</ object > Embedding covers the other ways, sizes that follow the page, and fallbacks. # What next Save your choices as a preset (bottom of Advanced ), or tick Remember settings in the FLA . Make it start on a click, on hover, when visible or with the scroll . Make it smaller: Performance . Export without Animate next time: tick Keep the scene data and use the command line .

The panel The panel works on the document in front of you. Its sections fold away; it remembers which are open and every setting, per user — and, if you like, inside the FLA. Every setting has a small i at the right: point at it (or reach it with the Tab key) for a short explanation, click it to keep the explanation open; its link leads to the matching part of this guide. An explanation, pinned by a click. # The top bar The document name shows what will be exported. Presets… applies a set of settings at once. Built in: Web animation (SMIL) , CSS animation , Interactive (JS player) , Still frames , Smallest file and Inkscape / Illustrator (static) . Your own presets appear below them (save them in Advanced ). Export runs the export. While it runs, a progress bar shows what it is doing and Cancel stops it — your document is never touched either way. # Output Setting What it does Format How the file animates: Automatic , SMIL , CSS , JS player , Frames , Lottie , .lottie , GIF , WebP . See Formats . File Where to write. Empty: next to the FLA, named after it. A name without a folder goes next to the FLA; a folder (ending in ``) gets the FLA s name inside it. The extension follows the format (a name ending in .svg becomes .json for Lottie; any other is kept and the format s added). The folder button opens a save dialog. Source Current timeline (the scene or symbol you are in), Selected library symbols (one file per symbol, named file _ symbol ; select them in the Library first — good for icon sets), or All scenes in a row , shown when the document has several scenes: they play one after the other as in Flash, and gotoAndPlay(5, Scene 2 ) , nextScene() and prevScene() jump between them. Frames All ; Current frame (always a still SVG); or a Range (first and last frame, 1-based). # Animation Setting What it does Smooth tweens On: tweens are interpolated between frames, as smooth as the screen allows (the high frame rate look). Off: one step per frame, exactly like the SWF. Loop Follow timeline plays as Flash would: frame scripts ( stop() , gotoAndPlay() ) decide; without them the timeline loops. Always loop and Play once override the scripts. Start Automatically , On click , On hover , From script (your page starts it), When visible (once half of it is on screen), On scroll (the scroll position drives it). See Interactivity . Scroll range With On scroll : While fully visible , While crossing the screen or With the whole page . Delay Seconds before it starts. Poster First frame or Last frame : shown where animation doesn t run, and to visitors who asked for reduced motion. Still poster for reduce motion On by default: visitors who turned animations off in their system see the poster, still. Start: On scroll, with its range. # Graphics text Setting What it does Include stage colour Paints the stage background. Off: transparent, so the page shows through. Embed images and sounds On: everything in one file. Off: bitmaps and sounds are written next to it ( bitmaps/ , sounds/ ) and linked — smaller SVG, more requests. Dynamic text as outlines Draws dynamic and input text as shapes, exactly as Animate does. Off (default): it stays real, selectable text. Embed fonts The fonts of dynamic text go into the file as small WOFF2 subsets of the letters used. See Text and fonts . Include hidden layers Hidden layers are exported (as Flash publishes them by default). Untick to leave them out. Include guide layers Guide layers are never shown in Flash; tick to export them anyway. # Images Sets how bitmaps are written: the format for lossy pictures ( JPEG , WebP , AVIF ), for lossless ones ( PNG , WebP lossless ), the Quality (0 = each bitmap s own setting from Animate) and the Resolution — bitmaps shown smaller than their pixels are written smaller, by default down to twice the largest size they appear at. The list shows every bitmap: choose Lossy or Lossless per picture, or Full to keep all its pixels. Details in Images and sounds . Images: formats, quality, resolution and every bitmap. # Sounds Only the JS player plays sounds. Choose MP3 or Opus for compressed sounds and a bit rate (0 = each sound s setting from Animate). Each sound follows its compression in Animate, or choose Compressed or Uncompressed (WAV) for it. Sounds: format, bit rate and every sound. # Advanced Setting What it does Size Stage size (fixed), or filling the space the page gives it like Flash s scale modes: Fill the space, show all , …no border (cropped), Stretch to the space . Decimals Precision on screen (default 2). Parts shown larger get more decimals, parts shown smaller fewer. Indent output Readable, bigger files. Compressed .svgz Gzipped SVG for design tools and servers set up for it. On the web, plain SVG compressed by the server is better ( why ). Remember settings in the FLA Stores the settings inside the document: whoever opens it gets them. Open in browser after export Shows the file right away. Keep the scene data (for the command line) Writes what the exporter read from Animate next to the output, as name .scene/ . The command line exports it again with other settings, without Animate. Presets Save the current settings under a name; delete your presets; Reset all settings . Graphics text and Advanced. # Result After an export: the number of files, their size and the time it took; Open in browser and Show file ; the size overview; a preview; and the lists of images, sounds and warnings. The size overview splits the bytes into drawing, animation, images, sounds, fonts, runtime and linked files, and names the biggest drawings (for example Scene 1 › fbf: 38.5 KB (150 drawings) ). The preview plays the file as a browser would; scrub it with the slider. A Lottie or .lottie export plays in lottie-web or the dotLottie player (pick one); a .lottie with a click start waits for a click on the preview. Warnings explain what could not be reproduced exactly. Most are about features a format can t have, for example sounds outside the JS player. A Lottie export in the preview.

Choosing a format The same timeline can be written in nine ways. They differ in where they play, what they can do and how big they get. The demo below is one export; switch the tabs to compare. # At a glance Format Plays in img Interactive Best for SMIL yes links, button states, start on click / hover / visible / scroll anything that just plays; the smallest file for tweens and shape tweens CSS yes links, button states, pause or restyle from your page, scroll-driven (inline) pages you control with CSS; smooth on weak devices JS player first frame only everything: buttons, code snippets, sounds, play() / gotoAndPlay() interactive pieces, sound, banners with logic Automatic as chosen as chosen when you don t want to decide Frames yes (still) – design tools, sprite sheets, print GIF / WebP yes – e-mail and places without SVG animation Lottie / .lottie – through the player s API iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native, lottie-web # SMIL SVG s own animation elements ( animate , animateTransform , set ). Eases become exact keySplines curves, so a tween with one ease is one short animation — no frames. Shape tweens become one drawing whose path changes. It plays in every current browser, inside img , object or inline, and in many apps that show SVG. Use SMIL by default. It is usually the smallest file and needs no script. Buttons get their Over and Down states from CSS, Go to Web Page snippets become links, and the start modes work ( click and hover everywhere, when visible and on scroll where scripts run). # CSS CSS @keyframes on each animated element, using the individual translate , rotate and scale properties, cubic-bezier() eases and linear() for curves that one bezier can t follow. Browsers run transform and opacity animations on the compositor, so CSS output stays smooth when the page is busy. It is made for browsers from 2023 on ( linear() : Chrome and Edge 113, Firefox 112, Safari 17.2); older ones use the closest classic timing for those curves, so nothing stands still. Pick CSS when your page wants to control the animation: animation-play-state: paused pauses it, your stylesheet can recolour it, and scroll-driven animations ( animation-timeline ) work when the SVG is inline. CSS can t change path data in Safari, so shape tweens are drawn frame by frame here (SMIL morphs them). # JS player The artwork plus a compact timeline and a small runtime (15.2 KB; with sound 18.7 KB) that plays it with Flash s own rules: frame scripts, movie clips that keep running after the main timeline stops, buttons with Up , Over and Down states, the mouse handlers that Animate s Code Snippets panel writes, and frame sounds with their sync, loops and envelopes. Your page can control it: play() , stop() , gotoAndPlay( label ) , seek(seconds) — see Player API . Scripts don t run in img , so put the file in an object , inline it, or use the flash2svg-player element. # Automatic Picks for you: the JS player when the animation needs it (sounds, mouse handlers from code snippets), otherwise CSS — or SMIL when SMIL is clearly smaller (more than 15 % smaller, typical for shape tweens). The result s warnings say which one it chose and why. # Frames One still SVG per frame ( hero_1.svg , hero_2.svg , …), or one for Current frame . Good for design tools — the Inkscape / Illustrator (static) preset draws text as outlines too — and for sprite sheets. # GIF and WebP Animated pictures for places where SVG doesn t animate: e-mail clients, chat apps, old CMSes. GIF has 256 colours per frame and plays everywhere. WebP keeps full colour and transparency and is usually much smaller; current mail clients and browsers show it — lossless for flat drawings (exact, and smaller than lossy there), lossy at the image quality for gradients and photos, chosen by the export. Both hold the first pass of the animation as the SVG formats play it — movie clips that keep running on a one-frame timeline or after a stop() included — at most 1500 frames, and repeat it from the start (a part that plays once before a loop comes again; warned). Above 50 frames a second a GIF leaves out a picture now and then (browsers would show very short frames for a tenth of a second), keeping its length. # Lottie and .lottie Lottie JSON for lottie-web and the native players on iOS, Android, Flutter and React Native, and .lottie — a dotLottie archive with the animation, its images and a state machine that plays it as your Loop and Start settings say. See Lottie and dotLottie . # Sizes compared Measured on this guide s demos (gzipped, the way a server sends them): Demo SMIL CSS JS player Lottie Nested gears 1.8 KB 1.8 KB 8.2 KB 2.8 KB Shape morph 25 KB 30 KB 31 KB 36 KB Easing 3.6 KB 3.6 KB 10 KB 8.0 KB Hero 6.1 KB 13 KB 13 KB 6.5 KB The JS player s numbers include its runtime: 6.2 KB of the gzipped size (more with sounds, shape tween morphs or mouse handlers).

Lottie and dotLottie Animate has no Lottie export of its own. Flash2SVG writes the same timeline as Lottie (a .json file) or .lottie (a dotLottie archive: the animation, its bitmaps and a state machine in one compressed file). Every test document is checked frame by frame in three players — lottie-web, dotLottie (ThorVG) and Skottie — against the SVG output, and validated with the official Lottie schema. # Which players Player Plays Notes lottie-web .json The web player; SVG or canvas renderer. dotLottie (web, iOS, Android, React, Flutter) .json and .lottie All drawn by ThorVG; run the state machine. Skottie (Skia / CanvasKit) .json Chrome s and Flutter s Lottie engine. lottie-ios, lottie-android .json (and .lottie ) Airbnb s native players. # What carries over Symbols become precompositions and keep their eases as Lottie keyframe curves. Movie clips that loop are drawn once and played again by a time remap . Frame scripts ( stop() , gotoAndPlay() ) are followed as in SMIL, and frame labels become markers: play a part with the player s marker or segment API. Masks become track mattes; shape tweens animated paths and gradients; colour effects (tint, brightness, advanced, alpha) go into the colours of the shapes inside, as Flash applies them. Bitmaps become image assets: embedded, written next to the JSON ( Embed images off), or inside the .lottie. Filters become layer effects: blur a Gaussian blur, drop shadow and glow a drop shadow (animated too), adjust colour goes into the colours. The filters Lottie has no effect for — inner, knockout and hide object shadows and glows, bevels, gradient glows and bevels, strong or uneven blurs — are built from track mattes, blend modes and blur or Tritone effects. In lottie-web and Skottie they match the SVG output exactly. Note Effects are not part of the Lottie specification 1.0, but lottie-web, dotLottie, Skottie and the iOS and Android players draw them. Other players may not. # Playing it // lottie-web: frame labels are markers const anim = lottie. loadAnimation ({ container: document. getElementById ( "hero" ), renderer: "svg" , loop: true , autoplay: true , path: "hero.json" , }); anim. goToAndPlay ( "intro" , true ); // dotLottie (npm @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web): the export's state machine plays it import { DotLottie } from "@lottiefiles/dotlottie-web" ; const player = new DotLottie ({ canvas: document. querySelector ( "canvas" ), src: "hero.lottie" , stateMachineId: "playback" , }); // with Start "From script": start it (again) player. stateMachineFireEvent ( "play" ); # Loops, intros and starting A Lottie JSON loops and autoplays as the player is told. When the timeline has an intro — it stops while movie clips keep running, or loops back to a label — the export has two markers, intro (play once) and loop (then loop it); the warnings say so. A .lottie carries a state machine called playback that plays it as your settings say: follow the timeline, loop or play once; start automatically, on a click, on hover or from script; show the Poster frame before a click or hover. dotLottie players run it when asked with stateMachineId: playback . # Buttons in a .lottie Mouse handlers from the Code Snippets panel become the state machine: every place playback can start (frame 1, jump targets, labels the buttons go to) is a state, clicks on the buttons layers are the transitions, and Go to Web Page becomes an OpenUrl action. Mouse over and out, and handlers in nested timelines, aren t followed (warned). # What is not in Lottie Feature In Lottie Sounds left out (warned) Button states ( Over , Down ) left out; use a .lottie state machine for clicks Editable text drawn as outlines; text field borders, filters and links are left out (warned) Subtract and add blends approximated (multiply by the inverted colours, screen) Hairlines keep the width they have at the scale their symbol starts with Bitmaps without smoothing drawn smoothed Colour effects on bitmaps tint and brightness exact; other colour effects keep only their alpha # Size and speed Lottie JSON is wordier than SVG: the test documents take 2303 KB as Lottie and 1310 KB as SMIL — gzipped 509 KB and 391 KB, and 564 KB as .lottie archives. Players draw a precomposition again for each use, so built filters cost render time: about 0.5–2 ms per shadow and 6–9 ms per bevel and frame in Skottie at 500×400. The players differ a little (measured): lottie-web blurs drop shadows slightly less than the others; dotLottie (ThorVG) blurs narrower, draws thin seams between the tiles of a repeating bitmap fill and fades the edges of a clipped bitmap fill.

Animation Flash2SVG reads the timeline the way Flash plays it, and checks every tween against the frames Animate itself draws. When its compact description reproduces every frame, it writes that; when it doesn t (anything unusual), it writes Animate s frames instead. # Tweens and easing Classic tweens and motion tweens (object-based) export with their real easing. Animate s −100…100 ease is a quadratic curve and comes out exact. Custom ease curves with any number of points — including overshoot, elastic and bounce shapes — and separate curves per property (position, rotation, scale, colour, filters) become exact Bézier pieces, not baked frames. Smooth tweens (on by default) interpolates between frames at the screen s rate. Turn it off for one step per frame, exactly like the SWF — the limited animation look. Rotations ( CW , CCW with a number of turns, Auto ) and tweens of colour effects and filters are all covered. # Motion guides A classic tween on a guided layer follows the curve drawn on its motion guide — any stroke, drawn with the pencil, the pen or as lines bent into curves. Orient to path turns the symbol with the curve. The guide layer itself isn t exported; draw the curve on a normal layer too if it should show. In SMIL, CSS and Lottie the motion is written along the curve itself (SMIL animateMotion , CSS offset-path , Lottie position keys with curved tangents): the symbol stays on the curve between frames too, at any frame rate, and the file is about half the size of a position per frame. The pace along the curve is Animate s own — checked at every frame, eases included — and so is the turning with Orient to path . Several tweens along one guide, keyframes held on it in between, guides inside symbols and looping movie clips are all covered. Animate s frames are written instead where that doesn t fit: an instance with a keyframe beside the curve (Animate snaps the transformation point onto the guide; a keyframe placed off it jumps there), a guide that is closed or has several strokes, and Smooth tweens off. The JS player, GIF and WebP use Animate s frames anyway. CSS motion paths need Safari 15.4, Chrome 55 or Firefox 72 or later. # Shape tweens In SMIL and the JS player a shape tween is one drawing whose paths, colours and gradients blend from the start shape to the end shape, just as Animate s in-betweens do. Flash2SVG matches up the frames Animate writes (contours that start at another point, curves written as lines, holes in another order, edges that shrink to nothing), fits the start and end shape to all of them and checks every frame. Frames that don t fit stay drawings of their own. Gradients that turn during the tween turn in SMIL too. The morph test document takes 105 KB as SMIL instead of 339 KB frame by frame (16 instead of 36 KB gzipped). --no-morph on the command line draws every frame instead. # Symbols Movie clips run on their own timeline from the moment they appear, and keep running across the parent s loop — also after the main timeline stops, as in Flash. Graphic symbols follow the parent s timeline with their loop mode: Loop , Play once , Single frame , and the reverse modes, with first and last frame. Buttons show their Up , Over and Down states (SMIL and CSS through CSS, the JS player exactly). See Interactivity . A symbol is written once and reused wherever it appears; only its transform and colour are per instance. # Masks Mask layers clip their masked layers — also animated masks, masks of several shapes, masks made of symbols and text, and masks inside symbols. # The camera Animate s camera — pan, zoom and rotation, tweened — exports as a transform of the whole stage. Its colour effects (tint, colour filter) aren t exported (warned). # Frame scripts Frame scripts aren t run as code, but the playback commands in them are followed — in AS3 and HTML5 Canvas syntax: In a frame script Exported as stop(); the timeline stops there (movie clips inside keep running) play(); it plays on gotoAndPlay( loop ); , gotoAndStop(12); a jump (labels and frame numbers; Canvas frames count from 0) gotoAndPlay( loop ) on the last frame an intro that plays once, then the loop if (n 3) gotoAndPlay(1); else stop(); play three times, then stop — Animate s snippet works too gotoAndPlay(1, Scene 2 ) , nextScene() with All scenes in a row Other conditions always run (warned), and a jump to a label that doesn t exist is left out (Flash stops the script there). # Layers and more Layer folders , hidden layers (exported by default, as Flash publishes them), guide layers (left out), guided layers. Layer parenting (Animate 2020+): children follow their parent s rig frame by frame. Advanced layers with layer effects: a colour effect, filters and a blend mode on a whole layer. 9-slice scaling of movie clips: corners keep their size, also in tweens (rotated instances scale normally, as in Flash). 3D rotations (rotation X/Y) export as their 2D projection. Video components (FLVPlayback, HTML5 Canvas Video ) become an HTML video over their place, the file copied next to the SVG.

Filters, blends and colour # Filters All of Animate s filters export, also tweened: blur , drop shadow , glow , bevel , gradient glow , gradient bevel and adjust colour — with inner , knockout and hide object , any quality, any strength. They are checked against Animate s own rendering and match within a fraction of a percent of the pixels. Two things work as in Animate, which can surprise: Filters follow the stage s orientation : the shadow of a rotated symbol doesn t turn with it, and blur sizes don t scale with it. Inside a rotated parent symbol they turn with the parent. A low-quality blur (one pass) is a box in Animate, with straight edge ramps; SVG and Lottie blur with a Gaussian of the same spread, so strong one-pass gradient glows look a little softer. In Lottie, blur, drop shadow and glow become effects; the others are built from mattes and blend modes — see Lottie . # Blend modes Normal , layer , multiply , screen , overlay , hard light , lighten , darken , difference , add , subtract , invert , alpha and erase . Alpha and erase act inside a symbol placed with the layer blend, as in Animate: they cut into what lies below them in that symbol. In Lottie, subtract and add are approximated (warned). # Colour effects Brightness , tint , alpha and advanced colour effects, tweened or not. Note Alpha on a symbol applies to each shape inside , as in Flash: where shapes overlap — the inner half of a stroke over its fill — they show through each other. Flash2SVG does the same. Inside such a symbol, alpha on nested symbols applies to them as a whole (SVG can t multiply inherited alpha per shape). # Fills and strokes Solid fills, linear and radial gradients (focal point, repeat and reflect , Linear RGB interpolation — also on strokes and in shape tweens), bitmap fills repeated or clipped (Animate stretches the edge pixels of a clipped fill; so does the export). Strokes with every cap and join, gradient strokes , and Animate s stroke styles (dashed, dotted, ragged, stipple, hatched — Animate s own SVG export turns the last three into many small shapes, so they get big). Hairlines and strokes with scale None keep their width when the symbol is scaled. Animate never draws a stroke thinner than one pixel; SVG does. A stroked symbol scaled far down — a card flipping through scale 0 — shows thinner outlines than in Animate. Strokes that scale only horizontally or vertically are drawn like Normal (warned). # Bitmaps Bitmaps — on stage, in symbols, as fills — export with their smoothing setting (pixel art stays crisp). How they are compressed is up to you: Images and sounds .

Text and fonts # Static text Static text is drawn as outlines , exactly as Animate draws it — no font needed to view it. Its words stay in the file as an accessible label, so screen readers read it (as Flash did) and search engines see it. # Dynamic and input text Dynamic and input text stay real text : selectable, searchable, read aloud, and changeable by your page s scripts. Flash2SVG brings the fonts along: it finds the installed font files by name (Windows, macOS and Linux folders, also font collections); cuts them down to the characters the text uses (HarfBuzz s subsetter, as WebAssembly, without hinting); embeds them as WOFF2 in an @font-face rule — Arial for 24 characters takes 2.6 KB . The text is laid out by the font s own metrics like Animate does: baselines from its ascent and descent, multiline fields wrapped at the field s width — within 1–2 pixels of Animate. Input fields carry all of Latin-1, so typing works. Fonts whose licence forbids embedding (the font s fsType ) and fonts that aren t installed are left to the viewer s fonts, with a warning. Untick Embed fonts to leave all of them out, or tick Dynamic text as outlines to draw dynamic text as shapes too. The size overview shows the fonts as a part of their own. # Text field settings In Animate In the SVG Show border around text a white field with a black outline behind the text Filters on a text field (a drop shadow on a heading) applied as on a symbol, in the stage s orientation A link on the text ( Properties › Options › Link and Target ) the field becomes a link (one per field) Password input fields a star per character — the text itself never leaves Animate Multiline , Multiline no wrap , Single line wrapped at the width only for Multiline Instance name data-name= … for your page s scripts Change a dynamic field from your page: const svg = document. querySelector ( "object" ).contentDocument; svg. querySelector ( '[data-name="score"] tspan tspan' ).textContent = "42" ; # In Lottie, GIF and WebP Lottie has no editable text that every player shows the same way, so all text is drawn as outlines there; text field borders, filters and links are left out (warned). GIF and WebP draw text as outlines too.

Images and sounds # Images Every bitmap is written either with loss (photos) or exactly (icons, pixel art, patterns). By default Animate s own setting decides — Library › Properties › Compression : Photo (JPEG) bitmaps are compressed with their quality, Lossless (PNG/GIF) ones keep every pixel. Change it per bitmap in the panel s Images section, and choose the formats: Formats Notes Lossy (photos) JPEG (default), WebP , AVIF JPEG at Animate s quality uses Animate s own JPEG, so imported JPEGs stay byte for byte. A photo with transparency is written as WebP (JPEG has none). AVIF s quality is scaled to look like JPEG at the same number. Lossless PNG (default, optimised), WebP lossless Every pixel stays the same, also the colour of transparent ones. Quality 0 uses each bitmap s own quality from Animate. Pictures that come out smaller without loss (small icons, flat graphics) stay lossless. In browsers, WebP works everywhere current; AVIF in about 93 % of them (2026). # Resolution A bitmap that is only ever shown smaller than its pixels — scaled down, inside scaled symbols, in tweens, under the camera, as a bitmap fill — is written smaller: down to twice its largest size on stage by default ( Resolution 2×, sharp on HiDPI screens and when the SVG is shown at twice its size). The other choices are 1×, 1.5×, 3× and Every pixel . Every frame and nesting level counts, so a bitmap is never written smaller than it is shown; it is still drawn at its full size, so nothing moves. Pixel art (no Allow smoothing ), repeating bitmap fills and bitmaps whose smaller file wouldn t be smaller keep every pixel; tick Full in the list for others. A 12-megapixel photo shown at 20 %: JPEG 1042 KB → 100 KB, AVIF 133 KB → 13 KB — and the export gets faster. The Result lists the format, pixels and size of every bitmap. # Sounds Frame sounds play in the JS player , with Animate s sound settings: Event , Start , Stop and Stream sync, Repeat and Loop , the effects and custom envelopes ( Edit sound envelope : volume and panning), in and out points, sounds in movie clips and on button states. Stream sounds follow the playhead, also after gotoAndPlay() or a pause. Formats Notes Compressed MP3 (default), Opus Bit rate from Animate s MP3 setting (otherwise 128 kbps stereo, 64 mono, less for low sample rates), or one for all. Opus sounds as good at half the bit rate; it plays in all current browsers, Safari from 18.4. Imported MP3s at their own quality stay byte for byte. Uncompressed WAV Sounds set to Raw in Animate (at its sample rate), or chosen per sound. Every sound is cut to the part the frames play : Animate pads its sounds with silence (a 0.4 s beep came out as a 3.7 s file). Convert stereo to mono is followed. Note Browsers block sound until the visitor clicks or presses a key. Until then the sounds run on silently and join at their position — a long one starts in the middle. SMIL, CSS, Lottie, GIF and WebP don t play sounds (warned). The encoders — the Squoosh codecs for images, LAME, libopus and mpg123 for sound — are WebAssembly builds that load only when a document has bitmaps or sounds. # Linked instead of embedded Untick Embed images and sounds ( Graphics text ) to write bitmaps and sounds next to the SVG ( bitmaps/ , sounds/ ) and link them: the SVG gets much smaller, the page makes more requests. Linked images don t show when the SVG is used as an img (browsers load nothing from inside an image) — embed them for that.

Interactivity # Start modes Animation › Start decides when the animation begins. Start What happens Where Automatically plays at once everywhere On click waits for a click on it; a click later starts it again SMIL, CSS, JS player, .lottie On hover starts when the pointer comes over it SMIL, CSS, JS player, .lottie From script waits for your page (see Player API ) SMIL, CSS, JS player, .lottie When visible starts once half of it is on screen (or it fills half the screen) where scripts run: inline, object ; in img it just plays On scroll the scroll position runs it, once, first frame to last see below Delay waits that many seconds before starting. # On scroll The page s scrolling plays the animation forwards and backwards. Scroll range says over which stretch: While fully visible — from the moment it is all on screen until it starts to leave (or, when it is taller than the screen, while it covers it); While crossing the screen — from entering at the bottom to leaving at the top; With the whole page — the page s whole scroll. Inline in a page, CSS output uses the browser s scroll-driven animations ( view-timeline and animation-timeline : Chrome and Edge from 115, Safari 26, current Firefox), which run off the main thread. Where they can t follow the page — in an object or iframe of the same site, inside a box with overflow: hidden (a view timeline follows its nearest scrolling box, and that one never scrolls), in older browsers — a few lines of script set the time from the scroll position instead. SMIL and the JS player always do it by script. Opened by itself, in an img or in a frame of another site, it just plays: no script there can see the page. # Buttons Button symbols keep their Up , Over and Down states. In SMIL and CSS output the states switch with CSS :hover and :active , so they work wherever the SVG is interactive (inline or in an object ). The JS player follows them exactly, Hit area included. # Code snippets The mouse handlers that Animate s Code Snippets panel writes into frame scripts run in the JS player — in AS3 and HTML5 Canvas documents: stop (); btn_play . addEventListener ( MouseEvent . CLICK , fl_ClickToGoToAndPlayFromFrame); function fl_ClickToGoToAndPlayFromFrame ( event : MouseEvent ) : void { gotoAndPlay ( "bounce" ); } Recognised: Events click, double click, mouse over and out (also roll over and out), mouse down and up — on the timeline itself or its named instances Syntax btn.addEventListener(MouseEvent.CLICK, …) , this.btn.addEventListener( click , ….bind(this)) , .on( click , …) , function literals and arrows Actions gotoAndPlay() / gotoAndStop() (frame or label), play() , stop() , nextFrame() , prevFrame() on this timeline, the root, the parent or named instances ( MovieClip(this.root) , exportRoot , this.parent , event.currentTarget ); instance.visible = true / false ; Go to Web Page ( navigateToURL(new URLRequest(…)) , window.open(…) ) Other code in a handler is warned about. Instances with click handlers show the hand cursor and can be reached with Tab and clicked with Enter or Space . In other formats: SMIL, CSS and still frames turn Go to Web Page into an SVG link and warn about the other handlers. A .lottie gets them as its state machine (see Lottie ). Automatic picks the JS player when a document has mouse handlers. # Links Links set on text ( Properties › Options › Link ) make the text field a link in every SVG format, and Go to Web Page snippets link their button. Links work inline and in an object ; in an img nothing is clickable.

Player API A JS player export plays by itself; your page can also control it. The API sits on the svg element as svg.flash2svg , and the element dispatches a flash2svg:ready event when it is set up. # Getting hold of the player // inline SVG const anim = document. querySelector ( "#hero svg" ).flash2svg; // in an <object>: once it has loaded const obj = document. querySelector ( "object#hero" ); obj. addEventListener ( "load" , () => { const anim = obj.contentDocument.documentElement.flash2svg; anim. gotoAndPlay ( "intro" ); }); # Methods and properties play() plays (a timeline that ran to its end without looping starts again) pause() holds everything: timelines, tweens, sounds stop() stops the main timeline, like stop() in a frame script — movie clips keep running gotoAndPlay(target) / gotoAndStop(target) jumps to a frame label or a 1-based frame number seek(seconds) sets the time from the start, deterministically (frame scripts and all); negative is 0, NaN and Infinity are ignored. Far ahead it finds where the animation repeats instead of playing every frame through currentFrame , totalFrames the main timeline s frame (1-based) and length speed playback speed, a positive number (1 = normal); other values are ignored muted turns the sounds off and on clip(name) a named movie clip instance: { play, stop, gotoAndPlay, gotoAndStop } , or null on(type, fn) frame : { frame, label } on every frame the main timeline enters ( frame counts from 0); end : when a non-looping timeline reaches its end const anim = svg.flash2svg; anim. on ( "frame" , ( e ) => console. log (e.frame, e.label)); anim. on ( "end" , () => document.body.classList. add ( "intro-done" )); anim.speed = 0.5 ; anim. clip ( "door" )?. gotoAndStop ( "open" ); Tip With Start: From script , the export waits for your play() — handy when the animation should begin with something on your page. # Performance The player hands tweened transforms and alpha to the browser as Web Animations , which run on the compositor: the artwork stays rastered and is only moved, so the page doesn t repaint it every frame. A test scene of 150 tweened instances of a detailed drawing runs at about 110 frames a second (2,560 at 59 fps). Symbols with hairlines (strokes that keep their width) are moved by the player itself, since their outline changes with every transform. The player rests while it is out of view or in a background tab and goes on where it was — unless its sound is on, then it keeps playing like a video. # The web component flash2svg-player (2.2 KB) puts an exported SVG into your page inline , so its scripts run and scroll-driven CSS works, without you fetching and inserting it yourself. It loads the file when it comes near the screen ( loading= eager : at once) and shows its children until then. < script type = "module" src = "flash2svg-player.js" ></ script > < flash2svg-player src = "hero.svg" > < img src = "hero-poster.png" alt = "Our product in motion" > </ flash2svg-player > < script > document. querySelector ( "flash2svg-player" ) . addEventListener ( "load" , ( e ) => e.target.player?. play ()); </ script > flash2svg-player.js is an ES module; flash2svg-player.iife.js is the same as a classic script. Both come with every release . The element s player property is the API above (for JS player exports).

Embedding on a web page # Four ways SMIL / CSS JS player Scripts run Scroll-driven CSS img src= hero.svg ✓ first frame only – – object data= hero.svg ✓ ✓ ✓ – inline svg … /svg in the page ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ flash2svg-player src= hero.svg ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ As an image — the simplest, and enough for SMIL and CSS exports that just play: < img src = "hero.svg" alt = "Our product in motion" width = "640" height = "360" > An image is sandboxed: no scripts, no links, no loading of linked files, no clicks. When visible and On scroll simply play there. As an object — for the JS player, links and buttons: < object data = "hero.svg" type = "image/svg+xml" width = "640" height = "360" aria-label = "Our product in motion" ></ object > Inline — paste the file s markup into your HTML, or insert it with a script. Every export has its own id prefix, so several exports can sit in one page without their ids clashing. Scroll-driven CSS needs this (or the web component). The web component does the inlining for you, lazily — see Player API . # Size on the page By default ( Size: Stage size ) the SVG has the stage s width and height, and scales like any image when you give it another size in CSS — it s vector art. To make the animation fill whatever space the page gives it , choose one of Flash s scale modes in Advanced › Size : Size Like Flash s Fill the space, show all showAll the whole stage, letterboxed (in the stage colour when Include stage colour is on) Fill the space, no border noBorder covers the space, cropping what sticks out Stretch to the space exactFit distorted to fit exactly < object data = "banner.svg" type = "image/svg+xml" style = "width:100%;height:60vh" ></ object > # Reduced motion Visitors who turned animations off in their system settings ( prefers-reduced-motion ) see the poster frame, still — in SMIL and CSS output, and in the JS player until they click it. This is on by default ( Still poster for reduce motion ; --ignore-reduced-motion on the command line). For SMIL it adds a still copy of the poster frame that shares the drawings: a few percent of the file. Browsers apply the setting to images too. To be sure, offer a still picture: < picture > < source media = "(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)" srcset = "hero.svg" > < img src = "hero-still.svg" alt = "Our product" > </ picture > # Fallbacks For places where SVG animation doesn t run — e-mail clients above all — export GIF or WebP as well and serve those there. Renderers without CSS (design tools, image viewers) show the poster frame of CSS exports from their transform attributes. # Pausing and styling CSS exports A CSS export s animations are ordinary CSS animations, so your page can control them: /* pause every animation in the export until the user hovers */ .hero svg * , .hero svg { animation-play-state : paused ; } .hero:hover svg * , .hero:hover svg { animation-play-state : running ; } # Serving it Let the server compress SVG, JSON and the player s script — preferably with Brotli — and cache it: Server nginx brotli on; brotli_types image/svg+xml application/json; or gzip_types image/svg+xml application/json; Apache AddOutputFilterByType BROTLI_COMPRESS image/svg+xml application/json (mod_brotli) or DEFLATE (mod_deflate) GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare compress SVG automatically The 59 test documents as SMIL: 1310 KB, 391 KB gzipped, 357 KB with Brotli. See Performance for .svgz .

Accessibility # From Animate s Accessibility panel Whatever is set in Animate s Accessibility panel ( Window › Other Panels › Accessibility , ActionScript 3 documents) goes into every SVG format: In Animate In the SVG The document s Name and Description the SVG s title and desc ; role img , or group when parts of it are accessible themselves A symbol instance s Name the instance becomes an image with that name (what is inside counts as part of it) An instance s Description a desc Buttons role button , their Shortcut as aria-keyshortcuts and their Tab index Make object accessible off the instance, text field or whole document is hidden from screen readers Documents without these settings stay as they were, apart from the static text labels below. # Text stays readable Static text is drawn as outlines, but its words stay in the file as the label of that drawing, so screen readers read it as they did in Flash. Dynamic and input text stay real text (see Text and fonts ). Give an animation that is used as an image a good alt text on the page: < img src = "chart.svg" alt = "Sales rose 40 % from March to June" > # Keyboard In the JS player, instances with a click handler (from the Code Snippets panel) can be reached with Tab and clicked with Enter or Space , and they show the hand cursor. # Reduced motion Visitors who asked their system for less motion see the poster frame, still — see Embedding . The JS player plays when they click it.

Small and fast # Read the size overview After every export, the Result splits the file into its parts and names the heaviest drawings. Start there: Part What it is What makes it smaller drawing the shapes of every symbol and frame fewer points (Animate s Optimize curves ), symbols instead of copies, fewer frame-by-frame drawings animation tweens and their timing Smooth tweens with simple eases; fewer keyframes images embedded bitmaps WebP or AVIF, lower quality, Resolution 1× sounds embedded sounds Opus, a lower bit rate, mono fonts embedded font subsets fewer fonts and styles, or Embed fonts off runtime the JS player s script (6.2 KB gzipped) SMIL or CSS when you don t need the player linked files next to the SVG — Biggest drawings lists the symbols and layers whose shapes take the most, for example Scene 1 › fbf: 38.5 KB (150 drawings) — frame-by-frame animation is usually the first thing to look at. # Pick the format For tweens and shape tweens, SMIL is usually the smallest: an eased tween is one short animation, a shape tween one morphing drawing. CSS comes close for transforms and runs on the compositor (smooth on busy pages), but draws shape tweens frame by frame. Automatic takes CSS unless SMIL is more than 15 % smaller. See Sizes compared . Animations that repeat inside a longer loop — a spinner turning every 8 frames in a 120-frame scene — are written once with their own repeat, not unrolled. # Simplify what Animate hands over Reuse symbols : a symbol is written once, however often it appears. Prefer tweens to frame-by-frame drawing; prefer shape tweens to drawn in-betweens. Run Modify › Shape › Optimize on heavy imported artwork. Keep text that doesn t change as static text ; avoid many fonts in dynamic text. Stipple , hatched and ragged stroke styles turn into many small shapes in Animate s own export — use solid strokes where you can. # Images and sounds Bitmaps shown smaller than their pixels are already written smaller ( Resolution ). Beyond that, AVIF gives the same look as JPEG at a quarter to nine tenths of its size (measured; AVIF s quality is scaled so the same number looks alike), WebP looks better than JPEG at the same quality number but isn t always smaller on noisy photos, and tiny or flat pictures are often smallest lossless. The Result lists every bitmap s format and size — compare. For sounds, Opus sounds as good as MP3 at half the bit rate. See Images and sounds . # Decimals Advanced › Decimals (default 2) is the precision on screen : a part shown at a tenth of its size gets one decimal less, one shown at 8× one more; angles and scale factors get what the size of what they turn needs. One decimal is often enough for large, simple shapes; the Smallest file preset uses it. # Compression Let the server compress SVG — it shrinks to about a third. The 59 test documents as SMIL: 1310 KB, 391 KB gzipped , 357 KB with Brotli . .svgz ( Compressed .svgz , --svgz ) writes the SVG gzipped, for design tools and for servers that send .svgz files with Content-Encoding: gzip (Apache: AddEncoding gzip .svgz ). Browsers show it only then — not from disk, not from a server that sends just the type. For the web, keep plain .svg and let the server compress it. # Smooth playback CSS and the JS player move tweened symbols on the compositor; the artwork is rastered once and only moved. SMIL is smooth too in current browsers. Blur and glow are the most expensive things to draw, especially animated and large. A cached copy — Animate s Cache as bitmap — doesn t exist in SVG. Hairlines (strokes that keep their width) must be redrawn at every scale: avoid them in symbols that scale. The JS player rests while it is out of view or in a background tab. The JS player draws 150 tweened instances of a detailed drawing at about 110 frames a second, and 2,560 at 59 (measured in Edge).

Command line The panel s compiler also runs in Node.js 24 or later , on any system. It turns the scene data the panel reads from Animate into SVG, Lottie, GIF or WebP — so you can export the same scene again with other settings, in a build script, or on a machine without Animate. # Get the scene data In the panel, tick Advanced › Keep the scene data (for the command line) . Export once. Next to the output you ll find a folder name .scene/ with scene.json , the drawings Animate exported ( atlas/ ) and the document s bitmaps and sounds. Copy that folder anywhere; it is everything the compiler needs. # Run it Unpack flash2svg-cli.zip from the releases and run: node flash2svg.js hero.scene/scene.json # SMIL → hero.svg next to the folder node flash2svg.js hero.scene/scene.json -o out/hero.svg --format css --loop always node flash2svg.js hero.scene/scene.json --format player --sound-format opus node flash2svg.js hero.scene/scene.json --format lottie # → hero.json node flash2svg.js hero.scene/scene.json --format dotlottie -o hero.lottie --begin click --poster last node flash2svg.js hero.scene/scene.json --format webp --background node flash2svg.js hero.scene/scene.json --format static --frames 1-12 --svgz node flash2svg.js hero.scene/scene.json --image-lossy avif --image-lossless webp --image-mode "logo.png=lossless" After the export it prints what the size is made of: 1 file(s), 23.4 KB, 3.00s - C:\work\hero.svg drawing 8.1 KB, animation 14.9 KB, fonts 0.4 KB Wrong options get a message, not a stack trace, and the exit code is 1 — handy in scripts. # Options --name=value works as well as --name value . Option -o , --out file output file, or a folder (existing, or ending in / ) to write the default name into (default: document .svg , .json or .lottie next to the scene folder). A scene of several library symbols gives one file each, name _ symbol . --format f smil (default), css , player , static , lottie , dotlottie , auto , gif , webp --frames a-b frame range, 1-based, inclusive ( 1-24 , or one frame: 5 ) --loop m auto (follow stop() scripts), always , never --begin m auto , click , hover , manual (from script), visible , scroll --scroll-range r with --begin scroll : visible (default), crossing , page --delay s start delay in seconds --steps no interpolation between frames (one step per frame, like the SWF) --scale m fixed (default), fit (show all), fill (no border), stretch (exact fit) --background include the stage colour --link-images write images and sounds as files next to the output instead of embedding --image-lossy f bitmaps set to Photo in Animate: jpeg (default), webp , avif --image-lossless f bitmaps kept exactly: png (default), webp --image-quality q quality of lossy bitmaps, 1–100 (default: each bitmap s own from Animate) --image-mode name=m per bitmap (library name): lossy or lossless ; repeatable --image-resolution x write bitmaps shown smaller down to x times their largest size on stage (default 2; 0 = every pixel) --image-full name keep every pixel of this bitmap; repeatable --sound-format f compressed sounds (JS player): mp3 (default), opus --sound-bitrate kbps on MP3 s scale (Opus uses half); default: each sound s own --sound-mode name=m per sound: lossy or lossless (WAV); repeatable --text-outlines draw dynamic text as outlines --no-embed-fonts leave fonts to the viewer --no-hidden-layers skip hidden layers --guides include guide layers --poster first|last the still frame for reduced motion and places without animation --ignore-reduced-motion animate also when the system asks for reduced motion --no-morph shape tweens frame by frame --digits n decimals on screen, 0–6 (default 2) --id-prefix p start of every id (default: a short hash) --pretty indented output --svgz gzip-compressed SVG -h , --help the list above The compiler loads its WebAssembly codecs (images, sounds, fonts, the GIF/WebP renderer) from the wasm folder next to flash2svg.js , only when a scene needs them. Fonts for dynamic text are looked up in the system s font folders.

x: Limits and troubleshooting # Common problems # The panel isn t in Window › Extensions Restart Animate after installing. With the zip install, CEP s debug mode must be on ( Installation ); the signed ZXP doesn t need it. Animate 2022 or later is required. # Animate quits as soon as a document opens The Flash2SVG panel was saved as open in your workspace and then the extension was removed. Install it again, start Animate, close the panel, quit Animate — then remove it. See Remove it safely . # The animation doesn t move In an img , a JS player export shows only its first frame: use object , inline it or use flash2svg-player ( Embedding ). Start is On click , On hover or From script : it waits. The visitor s system asks for reduced motion : they see the poster on purpose. A stop() on frame 1 — the export follows your frame scripts. Loop: Always loop ignores them. Opened from disk as .svgz : browsers show .svgz only when a server sends it with Content-Encoding: gzip . # Scroll-driven CSS doesn t follow the scroll It follows the page inline, in an object or iframe of the same site and in flash2svg-player — also inside boxes with overflow: hidden and in browsers without scroll-driven animations (a script takes over). Opened by itself, in an img or in a frame of another site it just plays: scripts can t see the page from there. # No sound Only the JS player plays sounds, and browsers allow sound only after the visitor clicked or pressed a key on the page. # The text uses another font The font isn t installed on the machine that exported, or its licence forbids embedding — the warnings say which. Install it, or tick Dynamic text as outlines . # The file is big Read the size overview — Small and fast goes through each part. # An export takes long Most of the time is Animate handing over the drawings (the progress bar says Exporting artwork through Animate ); compiling takes milliseconds. Many frame-by-frame drawings, stroke styles like stipple and big shape tweens take longest. AVIF encoding of large photos takes a second or two each. # Known limits Frame scripts are not run: stop() , play() , gotoAndPlay() / gotoAndStop() with frame numbers or labels are followed; of conditions only pass counters ( if (n 3) gotoAndPlay(1); else stop(); ). Other conditional actions always run (warned). Mouse handlers from code snippets: see Interactivity ; keyboard, ENTER_FRAME and timer handlers aren t run (warned). Movie clips with loops of very different lengths (say 7, 11 and 13 frames in a 600-frame scene) can t all come round within one SMIL/CSS loop: SMIL and CSS repeat after the common period they find, so some clips jump when the animation repeats (warned). The JS player is exact. Shape tweens in CSS output are drawn frame by frame. Animate draws a shape tween s keyframe a little differently from the start of its morph; where they differ by more than a quarter pixel, the keyframe stays a drawing of its own. A shape that splits into several looks different in Animate s preview than in its SVG export; the export follows the SVG export. Strokes: Horizontal and Vertical scale options are drawn like Normal (warned). Animate never draws a stroke thinner than one pixel; SVG does. Alpha on a symbol applies to each shape inside, as in Flash; inside such a symbol, alpha on nested symbols applies to them as a whole. Groups that hold symbol instances are split: the group s drawing first, its instances above it. 9-slice: an animated scale is sliced frame by frame for symbols that only hold drawings; named instances and symbols with nested symbols keep normal scaling then (warned). 3D transforms export as their 2D projection. IK armatures and components other than video aren t exported. Video embedded in the timeline (FLV) isn t exported. The camera s colour effects (tint, colour filter) aren t exported. Lottie: sounds, button states and editable text are left out; subtract and add are approximated. lottie-web draws an inner gradient bevel only faintly (Skottie and dotLottie draw it right). See Lottie . Animate adds the temporary copy each export works on to its Recent files list (JSFL can t open a document without that). # Reporting a problem Open an issue with what you expected and what you got, the panel s warnings, and — if you can — the FLA or a small one that shows it. With Keep the scene data ticked, the .scene folder is often all that s needed to reproduce it.

What s new The full list is in the changelog ; downloads are on the releases page . # 4.3 Motion along guides. A classic tween on a motion guide now moves along the guide s curve itself in SMIL, CSS and Lottie, instead of from one frame s position to the next: smooth at any screen refresh rate, turned along the curve with Orient to path , at Animate s own pace, and about half the size (the path demo on Animation : SMIL −56 %, CSS −59 %). JS player: with Play once and a one-frame main timeline, movie clips no longer move one frame on before they hold. # 4.2.2 CSS fixed in Chrome and Edge. While a CSS export ran, Chrome and Edge drew some objects in the wrong place — an object that moves and scales at once, whose transformation point also shifts (the banner s button on Animation sat in the top-left corner).
